correctness.rationale: Let G=complement(H) for H=P_n or C_n, n≥5. With r initial whites, each blue vertex has r−|N_H(v)∩W|≥r−2 neighbors among whites in G, hence r≥4 immediately stalls; Z≥n−3. With r=2, path/cycle vertices u,w have distinct external H-neighborhoods, so some blue v sees exactly one of u,w in H and forces the other in G; remaining singleton is forced since δ(G)≥2. For r=3, first G-force happens iff a blue degree-two vertex of H has both its H-neighbors among the three whites, and then pair completion finishes. Path counting (n−2)(n−3) center–triple incidences minus n−4 double counts yields n²−6n+10. Cyclic incidences n(n−3), usually n double-center triples give n(n−4); at n=6 precisely two alternating triples have three centers and each causes multiplicity adjustment +2, giving n(n−4)+2. Thus full polynomials have low coefficient as displayed, then binom(n,2), n, 1; difference 2n−10+2*[n=6], zero at n=5. Independently enumerated all initial blue sets for n=5..10 in path/cycle complements, matched both polynomials (n=6 path 10, cycle 14 minimum sets). This bounded test does not prove all n; the incidence argument does.
